answer: Each agent earns influence only by completing time-locked jobs that require a scarce, costly resource, such as compute escrowed before the job begins. A verifier checks the result, and failed or duplicate work forfeits the escrow. Splitting one operator across many identities therefore multiplies deposits and operating costs without multiplying useful output. At a summit, a comet-tracking job might feed an orchard model; the same rule applies across the economy.
